title: Targeting Aggressive VHL Disease with a Germinal Mutation in the CHEK2 Gene: A Personalized Approach
content: Background: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) is a rare inherited dominant disorder leading to central nervous system hemangioblastomas, clear cell renal carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and pan-creatic tumors. It affects 1 in 36,000 births, VHL patients are heterozygous for a pathogenic VHL mutation in germline. A second mutation in the other allele is required for tumor development, resulting in loss of pVHL function, responsible for degradation of Hypoxia-Inducible Factor (HIF) under normoxia. Without pVHL, HIF translocates into nucleus, inducing targets of the hypoxia program, among them genes involved in proliferation and angiogenesis. VHL disease shows variable phenotypic manifestations and different severity. A previous study analyzed a severe case of VHL with an unusually early onset and aggressive progression, carrying a heterozygous Check2 mutation. Methods: Cell cultures from three surgeries of this patient were analyzed, revealing complete loss of pVHL and multiple somatic mutations in different tumor cells. Using the “Pandrugs” algorithm as a predictive tool and inputting VHL and CHEK2 as the mutated genes, Olaparib was identified as the most suitable therapeutic option. Olaparib is a poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor. Results: In vitro, olaparib reduced cell viability by 50%, moreover combined with ICI-118,551, a beta-adrenergic receptor blocker, viability was re-duced by 80%, showing an additive effect. Conclusions: These findings highlight the role of personalized medicine showing how tailored treatments can improve clinical outcomes.
